long_biography.plain_text:
At fifteen, Gina Addeo helped handle the post and phones at the Staten Island business Richard Addeo had started. She later studied engineering at Stevens and worked on computer systems used on financial trading floors. Returning to the electrical trade, she qualified for the city's master electrician's licence in 1993, the first woman to do so. That year she launched GMA Electrical, finding a separate niche and winning work from the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.

Seven years later, Addeo returned to the family company. She purchased 37.5% from Richard through an annuity arrangement, gaining an economic stake before she became chief executive following his death in 2005. The remaining family share passed to Lisa, who took on a different executive role. The sisters have since brought employees into ownership while continuing to direct the contractor. Gina also became the first woman to lead the local chapter of the National Electrical Contractors Association.
